newsitem.title: UK: IEA sees big rise in OPEC output, lower 1997 demand.
newsitem.headline: IEA sees big rise in OPEC output, lower 1997 demand.

text.p: Oil supply jumped in April due to a big increase in OPEC production but demand for the cartel's barrels remained stagnant despite lower than expected non-OPEC output, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.

The Paris-based agency revised down its estimate of world demand for 1997 by 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 73.6 million bpd, matching an identical downward revision to its estimate for non-OPEC output.

World oil supply grew by nearly 300,000 bpd to 74.6 million bpd in April, largely thanks to the 11-member Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) which lifted crude production by 220,000 bpd to 27.13 million bpd in April, the IEA said in its monthly Oil Market Report.

Forecast demand for oil from OPEC was revised up by 100,000 bpd in the second quarter because of slower than expected output growth from non-OPEC countries, but the West's energy watchdog held its 1997 average forecast at 25.3 million bpd.
The IEA said industry stocks in OECD countries rose by a sharp 500,000 bpd in March, largely due to a big build in the United States.
